name: Altstadt Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Largest preserved old town in Tyrol with late Gothic burgher houses, the Münzerturm tower, and the Upper Town Square – freely accessible.
beschreibung:
The old town of Hall in Tirol is one of the largest preserved historical complexes in Austria. The town lies ten kilometres east of Innsbruck and was first mentioned in records in 1256. In 1303, Hall received town rights with the same privileges as Innsbruck and rose to become the most important economic centre in North Tyrol. The foundation of its prosperity was salt, which was mined in the Halltal until 1967 and boiled at the Inn River.

From 1477, the sovereign mint was located in Hall, and in 1486 the world's first thaler was minted here. In 1567, the mint moved to Hasegg Castle with its 46-metre-high Münzerturm tower. After the town fire of 1447, Hall again comprised over 300 houses. Since 1973, the old town has been comprehensively revitalised, an achievement honoured in 1984 with the First Austrian State Prize for Monument Protection. Guided town tours take place year-round on Mondays, Thursdays, and Saturdays at 10 am.
